high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Vietnamese lacquer illustration: beside a Red River Delta water-puppet pavilion, one percussionist strikes a frog-marked wooden bell, the matching lacquered frog puppet rises from the pond, and two differently marked puppets remain motionless, so one specific cue releases only its waiting performer without labels or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A deep indigo pond fills the lower two-thirds beneath a black-and-vermilion water-puppet pavilion fixed across the upper field. One tight ring of pale ripples opens around the active center while the outer water remains still. Flat gold, red, green, indigo and eggshell-white shapes replace realistic depth. No photographic light, gradient, written banner, alphabet, numeral, caption, arrow, flowchart, screen, book, tablet, textile panel, throne, national flag or modern device appears.

elements.desc: The primary background element, a Red River Delta water-puppet pavilion fixed above the pond, built from vermilion columns, a dark tiled roof and a plain green bamboo curtain concealing the operators. Three low water openings face the stage at equal height; the structure carries no written banner, temple inscription, number, arrow, royal crest, ticket sign, screen or photographic detail.

Adult Vietnamese percussionist seated at the left edge of the pond, medium skin tone, straight black hair tied beneath a dark headcloth, plain ochre tunic, indigo trousers and bare feet. With an attentive neutral expression, both hands deliver one controlled mallet strike to the frog-marked wooden bell; no conducting baton, crown, badge, written score, microphone or command platform appears.

Low red-lacquered percussion stand before the musician, holding one green wooden bell carved with a simple three-lobed frog footprint, plus an untouched bronze gong marked by a crescent and closed cymbals marked by two parallel reeds. Only the frog bell meets the raised mallet; none bears text, number, arrow, magical rune, status light or electronic control.

Active wooden frog water puppet rising at center from the pond, painted leaf green with a cream belly, vermilion mouth and the same three-lobed footprint on its chest as the struck bell. Its lacquered body tilts forward above one compact ripple ring, visibly moving alone; it has no speech bubble, crown, sacred attribute, written label, arrow, wire or exposed operator.

Waiting wooden buffalo water puppet floating motionless near the right pavilion opening, painted matte black with ochre horns, a white crescent on its shoulder and a level horizontal body. The surrounding water remains unbroken and its matching bronze gong stays untouched; the puppet has no rider, rope, text, number, arrow, command badge, royal ornament or exaggerated expression.

Waiting wooden duck water puppet resting motionless near the lower-left water edge, painted ochre with a green neck, vermilion beak and two parallel reed marks on its side. Its body sits level without wake while the matching cymbals remain closed on the stand; it carries no caption, numeral, arrow, crown, religious emblem, visible control rod or duplicated companion.

Compact three-person village music ensemble seated at the upper-right beside the pavilion, medium skin tones, black hair, plain green, red and indigo tunics with dark trousers. A bamboo flutist and two singers watch the active frog while keeping their instruments at rest; no one signals the buffalo or duck, and no written score, microphone, podium, uniform badge or hierarchy appears.
